label: Bible Study
prompt: For in him we live, and _____, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.
verse: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.
note: Paul on Mars' Hill, quoting Greek poets to Athenians — meeting his audience where they lived.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who can be _____ us?
verse: What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who can be against us?
note: Paul's closing argument begins: if God is for us, the list of real threats gets very short.

label: Sunday School
prompt: When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the _____, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
verse: When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
note: The KJV says 'physician' where we'd say doctor — Jesus explaining why he keeps such company.

label: Deep Water
prompt: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye _____ thee.
verse: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.
note: Job's final confession: after all the debate, secondhand theology gave way to sight.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Be ye not _____ yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?
verse: Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?
note: 'Unequally yoked' — like an ox and an ass in one harness, which the Law forbade (Deuteronomy 22:10).
